properties.description:
At 759 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Pinon, or 16 miles north of Pueblo Airport, moving northeast at 50
mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Northeastern Pueblo, Pueblo Airport, Fountain, Boone, Hanover,
Avondale, Pueblo Depot, Pinon, and Pueblo West.
properties.instruction: If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

properties.areaDesc: Kane, UT; Washington, UT
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 7:55PM MDT until October 11 at 10:00PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
West Central Kane County in southern Utah...
East Central Washington County in southwestern Utah...

* Until 1000 PM MDT.

* At 755 PM MDT, National Park Service officials reported
thunderstorms producing heavy rain and flash flooding across Zion
National Park. Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen, with
little additional rainfall expected. Flash flooding is already
occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...National Park Service reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks, streams, slot
canyons, and normally dry washes.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Zion National Park, Springdale and Rockville.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 10:00 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 10:00 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 11 at 9:51PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor remains in Moderate Flood Stage due to
north winds and upstream heavy rainfall draining through the basin.
River levels are forecast to remain near the Moderate Flood Stage
threshold above Minor Flood Stage through most of this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Sunday the stage was 3.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Sunday was 3.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected remain steady around 3.1ft
through at least midweek.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Monday afternoon at 1215 PM EDT.

Raynolds pass, Henrys Lake and Targhee pass already have 1 to 2
inches of snow with sub-freezing temperatures. More snow is likely
in these areas through tomorrow morning. Look for 1 to 3 inches
of more snow possible tonight. Dry northerly flow over the Montana
Divide has held off the precipitation coming up from our south
recently. However, current radar imagery show light precipitation
making it to Henry's Lake. Please use caution when driving in
these areas.

* WHERE...Lower Snake River Plain and Upper Snake River Plain.

* WHEN...From 3 AM to 9 AM MDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Frost could harm sensitive outdoor vegetation. Sensitive
outdoor plants may be killed if left uncovered.
properties.instruction: Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 11 at 9:27PM EDT until October 12 at 11:00AM EDT by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Blacksburg has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Virginia...

New River at Allisonia affecting Pulaski and Wythe Counties.

For the New River...including Galax, Allisonia, Radford, Glen Lyn,
Hinton...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...New River at Allisonia.

* WHEN...Until Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, River begins to overflow the left bank and
affect Clarks Ferry Road, Route 653. Water may already cover part
of Julia Simpkins Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Sunday the stage was 7.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this evening to a crest of 8.4 feet just after midnight tonight.
It will then fall below flood stage tomorrow morning.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 8.4
feet on 01/08/1946.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

properties.areaDesc: Shoshone/Lava Beds; Arco/Mud Lake Desert; Upper Snake River Plain; Lower Snake River Plain; Eastern Magic Valley; Southern Hills/Albion Mountains; Raft River Region; Marsh and Arbon Highlands; Franklin/Eastern Oneida Region; Bear River Range; Bear Lake Valley; Blackfoot Mountains; Caribou Range; Big Hole Mountains; Teton Valley; Centennial Mountains/Island Park; Beaverhead/Lemhi Highlands; Sun Valley Region; Wood River Foothills
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 11 at 7:26PM MDT until October 12 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Pocatello ID
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central, eastern, south central, and southeast
Idaho, including the following areas, in central Idaho, Sun Valley
Region and Wood River Foothills. In eastern Idaho, Beaverhead -
Lemhi Highlands, Big Hole Mountains, Centennial Mountains - Island
Park and Teton Valley. In south central Idaho, Eastern Magic Valley
and Shoshone/Lava Beds. In southeast Idaho, Arco/Mud Lake Desert,
Bear Lake Valley, Bear River Range, Blackfoot Mountains, Caribou
Range, Franklin/Eastern Oneida Region, Lower Snake River Plain,
Marsh and Arbon Highlands, Raft River Region, Southern Hills/Albion
Mountains and Upper Snake River Plain.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A prolonged period of rainfall could lead to some flooding across
parts of the advised area. An upper low moving into the Pacific
Northwest will combine with tropical moisture from Tropical
Cyclone Rachel to usher in a cooler, wetter weather pattern
across eastern Idaho.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH MONDAY AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Clinton, IA; Scott, IA
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 11 at 8:23PM CDT until October 13 at 12:00AM CDT by NWS Quad Cities IA IL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Iowa...

Wapsipinicon River near De Witt 4S affecting Clinton and Scott
Counties.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring.

* WHERE...Wapsipinicon River near De Witt 4S.

* WHEN...Until late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Overbank flooding occurs. Water affects
residences along the river between Wheatland and Calamus. Water
affects businesses along the river near Calamus.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM CDT Sunday the stage was 12.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The river continues to fall rapidly.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tomorrow afternoon and continue falling to 8.1 feet Sunday,
October 18.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

The next statement will be issued by Monday evening.
